Article: Dang Anh-Hoang, Tran, V., & Nguyen, L.-M. (2025). Survey and analysis of hallucinations in large language models: Attribution to prompting strategies or model behavior.
Summary: Surveys hallucination causes in LLMs, categorising them by prompting strategies and model behaviour. Finds that LLMs fabricate outputs when information is missing rather than returning null.
Limitations/Gaps: Focuses on hallucination classification broadly, does not test mitigation strategies in specific extraction tasks like event parsing.

Article: Dennstädt, F. et al. (2025). A comparative performance analysis of regular expressions and a large language model-based approach to extract the BI-RADS score from radiological reports.
Summary: Compared Regex and LLM for extracting scores from radiology reports. Found Regex was over 28,000 times faster but could not handle all linguistic variations.
Limitations/Gaps: Domain-specific to radiology. Does not address informal or ambiguous text inputs like calendar event descriptions.

Article: Huang, K.-H. et al. (2024). TEXTEE: Benchmark, Reevaluation, Reflections, and Future Challenges in Event Extraction.
Summary: Benchmarked five LLMs across 16 event extraction datasets spanning eight domains. Found LLMs fall short of achieving reliable performance compared to fine-tuned models.
Limitations/Gaps: Datasets span news, biomedical, cybersecurity etc. but none reflect everyday productivity scenarios like calendar scheduling.

Article: Kataoka, Y. et al. (2025). Automating the data extraction process for systematic reviews using GPT-4o and o3.
Summary: Developed an open-source GPT-4o system for automated data extraction in systematic reviews. Achieved up to 96.3% overall accuracy but found accuracy was higher for string variables than numeric variables.
Limitations/Gaps: Authors concluded it cannot yet replace humans for numeric data extraction. Does not address calendar-specific fields like dates and times.

Article: Kumar, H. (2026). Hybrid Validation Agent: Rule-Based Engine + LLM Fallback.
Summary: Proposed a rules-first, LLM-fallback architecture for input validation. Reports 70% cost reduction and 80x speed improvement for predictable inputs.
Limitations/Gaps: Only tested on structured form validation and chatbot slot-filling. Whether this pattern generalises to complex domains like event extraction is untested.

Article: Latifi, P. (2025). Is "Hope" a person or an idea? A pilot benchmark for NER: comparing traditional NLP tools and large language models on ambiguous entities.
Summary: Compared LLMs against traditional NLP tools on ambiguous named entity recognition. Found LLMs outperform on context-dependent language but conventional systems are preferable for determinism and speed.
Limitations/Gaps: Pilot study focused on NER ambiguity, not event extraction or structured field extraction.

Article: Liu, P. et al. (2024). A Survey on Open Information Extraction from Rule-based Model to Large Language Model.
Summary: Surveyed the evolution of open information extraction from rule-based to LLM approaches. Found hallucination is a major challenge and suggested integrating rule-based methods into LLM frameworks improves reliability.
Limitations/Gaps: Broad survey covering open IE generally, does not provide empirical comparison data for specific extraction tasks.

Article: Marin, J. (2026). Hallucinations in LLMs Are Not a Bug in the Data.
Summary: Argued that hallucinations are an inherent architectural feature of Transformers, not a data quality issue that can be fully prompted away.
Limitations/Gaps: Opinion/analysis piece, not empirical research. Does not test or propose specific mitigation strategies.

Article: Nawalny, M. et al. (2025). Comparative Evaluation of GPT-4o, GPT-OSS-120B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct Language Models in a Reproducible CV-to-JSON Extraction Pipeline.
Summary: Compared three LLMs on CV-to-JSON extraction. Found open-weight models reached only 73-79% completeness compared to GPT-4o, revealing significant performance-cost trade-offs.
Limitations/Gaps: Focused on CV/resume extraction, not event extraction. Does not compare LLMs against rule-based alternatives.

Article: Suneja, S. (2026). Hybrid Extraction: When to Use LLMs vs Local Models vs Regex.
Summary: Discussed the practicality trade-offs of LLMs vs Regex for high-volume parsing, highlighting time inefficiency and token costs of LLMs.
Limitations/Gaps: Blog post, not peer-reviewed. Does not provide original experimental data.

Article: Viet Dac Lai (2022). Event Extraction: A Survey.
Summary: Comprehensive survey defining event extraction as identifying triggers and arguments (time, location, description) from natural language.
Limitations/Gaps: Published 2022, predates the generative LLM era (GPT-4 etc.) so does not cover LLM-based extraction approaches.
